sq.q: \(\text{For odd function in } (-\pi, \pi), \text{ what happens to Fourier coefficients?}\)
answer: \(\text{Series becomes sine series: } f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n \sin nx\)

sq.q: \(\text{Write Fourier series for function in } (-\pi, \pi) \text{ with coefficients formulas.}\)

lq.q: Find the Fourier series for \(f(x)=|\sin x|\) in \((-\pi,\pi)\).
answer: Step Marks Since \(f(x)\) is even, \(b_n=0\) (2) \(a_0=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\,dx=\frac{4}{\pi}\) (2) \(a_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\cos nx\,dx=\frac{2}{\pi}\cdot\frac{1+(-1)^n}{1-n^2}\) for \(n\neq1\) (4) For \(n=1\): \(a_1=0\) (2) Thus, \(|\sin x|=\frac{2}{\pi}-\frac{4}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\cos 2nx}{4n^2-1}\) (5)
